title: Proprietary Funds
description: Learn enterprise and internal service funds and how they use economic resources measurement and accrual accounting.
html:
Proprietary Funds

Proprietary funds account for government activities that operate in a manner similar to commercial businesses.

Unlike governmental funds, proprietary funds use:

ECONOMIC RESOURCES MEASUREMENT FOCUS + ACCRUAL BASIS OF ACCOUNTING

This means proprietary funds generally recognize assets, liabilities, revenues, and expenses similarly to business enterprises.

Two Types of Proprietary Funds

Enterprise Fund Provides Goods or Services Primarily to External Users
Internal Service Fund Provides Goods or Services Primarily to Other Government Departments

Enterprise Funds

Enterprise funds generally account for activities in which goods or services are provided to the public or other external users for a fee.

Enterprise fund reporting may also be required when applicable criteria are met, such as when laws, regulations, debt arrangements, or pricing policies require an activity's costs to be recovered primarily through fees and charges.

Common Examples
  • Public water utilities
  • Government-owned airports
  • Public transit systems
  • Government parking operations

Think:

Government + customers outside the government + user charges → Enterprise Fund.

Internal Service Funds

Internal service funds generally account for goods or services provided by one department or agency of a government to other departments or agencies, usually on a cost-reimbursement basis.

Example

A city's centralized motor pool maintains vehicles for the police, fire, and parks departments and charges those departments for the services.

The activity may be accounted for in an internal service fund.

EXTERNAL CUSTOMERS → ENTERPRISE INTERNAL DEPARTMENTS → INTERNAL SERVICE

Capital Assets

Because proprietary funds use the economic resources measurement focus, they generally report capital assets directly in the fund.

Capital assets are also generally depreciated.

Equipment Cost $300,000
Useful Life 10 Years
$300,000 ÷ 10 = $30,000 Annual Depreciation

This is very different from a governmental fund, where acquisition of equipment is generally reported as an expenditure rather than recording and depreciating the capital asset in the fund.

Long-Term Debt

Proprietary funds generally report their long-term liabilities directly because they use the economic resources measurement focus.

PROPRIETARY FUND Capital Assets ✓ Depreciation ✓ Long-Term Liabilities ✓

Revenues and Expenses

Proprietary fund statements distinguish operating activities from nonoperating activities.

Operating Examples

  • Charges to customers for services
  • Employee costs related to operations
  • Supplies and other operating costs

Nonoperating Examples

  • Interest revenue
  • Interest expense
  • Certain investment-related amounts

Proprietary Fund Statements

Proprietary funds generally present:

Statement of Net Position Financial Position
Statement of Revenues, Expenses, and Changes in Fund Net Position Operating Results
Statement of Cash Flows Cash Activity

Important Cash Flow Difference

Proprietary fund cash flow statements use categories that differ somewhat from those commonly seen in business accounting.

One important CPA distinction is that proprietary fund statements include an operating activities category based on governmental reporting requirements, along with noncapital financing, capital and related financing, and investing activities.

Governmental vs. Proprietary

Governmental Funds Modified Accrual + Current Financial Resources
Proprietary Funds Accrual + Economic Resources

CPA Memory Rule

ENTERPRISE = OUTSIDE USERS INTERNAL SERVICE = INSIDE USERS BOTH = ACCRUAL + ECONOMIC RESOURCES

Key Takeaways

  • Proprietary funds use accrual accounting.
  • They use the economic resources measurement focus.
  • Enterprise funds generally serve external users.
  • Internal service funds generally serve other government departments.
  • Proprietary funds report and depreciate capital assets.
  • They generally report their long-term liabilities directly.

quiz.prompt: A city operates a central vehicle maintenance department that primarily services vehicles used by the city's police, fire, and parks departments. Which fund is generally most appropriate?
quiz.explanation: An internal service fund generally accounts for goods or services provided primarily to other departments or agencies of the same government.
